JOURNAL

A late-night writing habit

2026.09.16

Songwriting is something Yu Stellar almost always saves for the night. There's too much noise during the day — commuting, conversations, to-do lists — it's hard to hear what actually needs to be said. Only once the city goes quiet is it possible to turn an ear inward.

It usually starts with a single line of lyric, or just the shape of a chord, quickly recorded on a phone — the sound quality doesn't matter, what matters is keeping that moment's feeling. A lot of the songs that eventually got finished started out as nothing more than a mumbled hum at two in the morning.

Listening back the next morning is often embarrassing, sometimes enough to make you want to delete it. But what survives tends to be the most honest line in the finished song. Things written late at night are always a little more willing to tell the truth.

If you're also the type who's especially awake late at night, maybe we're listening to the same frequency.
